title: The Principle of Superposition in Quantum Systems
text:
Quantum superposition dictates that a particle exists in all possible states simultaneously until it is observed or measured. Mathematically, this state is described by a linear combination of eigenvectors associated with the observable quantity.

The act of measurement compels the quantum system to collapse its wave function, instantaneously resolving the particle into a single, definite state. This reduction from potentiality to actuality represents one of the most counterintuitive aspects of modern physics and remains a subject of intense theoretical debate.
